Count the cells of each group before the bootstrap

Source: R/cells.R
trop_cells.Rd

trop_cells() shows which treated cells are in each group of trop_effects(), and which cells are not. It does not show the effects. Thus, you can examine the estimand before you see the results or calculate the bootstrap.

Usage

trop_cells(
  fit,
  by = c("event_time", "cohort", "time", "unit", "overall"),
  window = NULL,
  anticipation = 0L,
  weights = c("cell", "unit"),
  unit_weights = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'trop_cells'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

fit

A trop object from trop() or trop_matrix() with method = "local".

by

The groups. Refer to the section Groups.

window

An optional vector with 2 event times. The function uses cells with an event time from window[1] to window[2].

anticipation

The number of treated periods at the start of each run that come before the true start. Refer to the section Anticipation. The default 0 uses the first treated period as the start.

weights

Use "cell" or "unit". Refer to the section Weights.

unit_weights

An optional numeric vector with one weight of 0 or more for each unit. A named vector must have a value for each unit name of the fit. A vector without names must be in the order of the rows of the panel.

x

A trop_cells object.

digits

The number of significant digits to show.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame of class trop_cells with one row for each group and the columns n_units, n_cells, n_excluded, n_skipped, and share. The column n_excluded counts the treated cells with an outcome that are outside of the target. The column n_skipped counts the cells in the target that have no effect, because the untreated cells do not identify them or their fit failed. The attribute totals has the counts for all treated cells.

Details

The function uses the groups, the window, the anticipation, and the weights of trop_effects(). For each group, it counts the units and the cells in the estimate. It also counts the treated cells outside of the target of the fit, and the cells that the untreated cells do not identify. A group with only cells outside of the estimate is also in the result.

The column share is the weight of each group in the overall estimate: the mean of all cells in the window with the same weights. With equal weights for each cell, the share of a group is its number of cells divided by the number of cells in the estimate.

If no treated cell is in a group, the result has no rows. The attribute totals and the print method then show where the treated cells are.

See also

trop_effects(), trop_rollout()

Examples

sim <- trop_simulate(n_units = 20, n_periods = 12, n_treated = 6,
                     n_post = 4, design = "staggered", seed = 1)
sim$in_target <- sim$time <= 11
fit <- suppressWarnings(
  trop(sim, "y", "d", "unit", "time", lambda = c(time = 0.2, unit = 0.5, nn = 0.5),
       target = "in_target", se = "none", control = trop_control(threads = 1))
)
trop_cells(fit, by = "event_time")
#> TROP cells by event time
#>   Weights: each cell has the same weight.
#>  event_time n_units n_cells n_excluded n_skipped share
#>           0       4       4          2         0 0.667
#>           1       2       2          2         0 0.333
#>           2       0       0          2         0 0.000
#> Cells in the estimate: 6. The column share is the weight of each group in the overall estimate.
#> Treated cells that are not in the estimate: 6 outside of the target.
